item.title: ‘Some people did everything right’: I lost my home in the Great Recession. I rent in my 50s. Why is that judged as failure?
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: Walmart, Best Buy and other stores now use digital price tags. Critics say they could lead to different prices for different shoppers.
item.description: Store aisles are getting a digital makeover.
item.dc:creator: Genna Contino

item.title: Retire on 8% a year with little or no risk? How to use annuities the right way.
item.description: Market turmoil has created a remarkable opportunity in recent weeks for retirees and those seeking secure, stable income for life.
item.dc:creator: Brett Arends

item.title: My spouse was awarded $90,000 from my 401(k) in our divorce. How is that fair?
item.description: “I retired in 2020 and subsequently went through a divorce a few years later.”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: Everyone’s talking about Roth conversions, but here’s how few people really do them — and why you shouldn’t have FOMO about it
item.description: You have to do the math to figure out your best tax strategy in retirement, and converting might not be for you.
item.dc:creator: Beth Pinsker

item.title: This hot AI-fueled stock has been in a rut. It just beat earnings expectations by 36%.
item.description: A company beating earnings expectations by 36% and revenue expectations by 15% would usually see a postresults bump. But not for Bloom Energy, the fuel-cell maker that has flourished due to data-center demand.
item.dc:creator: Steve Goldstein

item.title: Young Americans are giving up on cars. It’s a path to financial freedom for some.
item.description: With vehicle prices soaring and ownership increasingly out of reach, some young adults are discovering that life without a car leaves them with breathing room to spend on other things.
item.dc:creator: Venessa Wong

item.title: Surging economy gets off to a good start in the fourth quarter — but there’s one big problem
item.description: Warning signs are emerging that consumers will be hit with rising prices.
item.dc:creator: Jeffry Bartash

item.title: ‘I don’t feel sorry for myself’: I’m 64 and will be renting for the rest of my life. Is that so bad?
item.description: “I married a wonderful man with a good income. He left his job due to health issues and suffered a massive stroke at 53.”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell

item.title: ‘She’s living the dream’: My stepmother said I can buy my childhood home for $850,000. Is she taking advantage of me?
item.description: “My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s.”
item.dc:creator: Quentin Fottrell
